problems.title: YetnotherrokenKeoard (Codeforces 1907B)
problems.description: A broken keyboard: 'b' deletes the last lowercase letter typed, 'B' the last uppercase one. Keep two stacks of positions to know what to delete. Difficulty 1000.

problems.title: Indian Summer (Codeforces 44A)
problems.description: Count the different leaves, where a leaf is a (tree species, colour) pair. Put std::pair values in a std::set and read its size. Difficulty 900.

problems.title: Sereja and Suffixes (Codeforces 368B)
problems.description: For many positions l, count the distinct numbers from l to the end. Walk from the back with a set and store each answer. Difficulty 1100.

problems.title: Powering the Hero (easy version) (Codeforces 1800C1)
problems.description: Each hero card takes the strongest bonus card collected so far. Keep the bonuses in a std::priority_queue. Difficulty 1000.

problems.title: Same Differences (Codeforces 1520D)
problems.description: Count pairs i < j with a[j] − a[i] = j − i. Rewrite it as a[i] − i = a[j] − j and count equal values with a map; the answer needs long long. Difficulty 1200.

exercises.title: Maximum Element (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Build a stack that can also report its maximum at any time. Hint: a second stack that remembers the maximum so far.

exercises.title: Queue using Two Stacks (HackerRank)
exercises.description: Build a queue (first in, first out) using only two stacks. A classic interview question.

exercises.title: Reverse Linked List (LeetCode 206)
exercises.description: Reverse a singly linked list by redirecting each node's next pointer. Draw the nodes on paper first.

exercises.title: Josephus Problem I (CSES)
exercises.description: Children in a circle; every second one leaves. Simulate it with a std::queue: move a child from the front to the back, then remove the next.

exercises.title: Last Stone Weight (LeetCode 1046)
exercises.description: Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones together. A std::priority_queue always hands you the heaviest.

exercises.title: Sum of Two Values (CSES)
exercises.description: Find two positions whose values add up to x, among up to 200,000 numbers. Remember each value's position in a map instead of checking every pair.

challenges.title: Data Structures: Stacks & Queues
challenges.description: Last in first out, first in first out, and linked nodes. Build a max-stack and a queue from stacks, reverse a linked list, simulate a circle with a queue, then fix a broken keyboard with stacks.

challenges.title: Data Structures: Sets, Maps & Heaps
challenges.description: Find things fast. Start with Last Stone Weight (priority queue) and Sum of Two Values (map), then the Codeforces problems from easiest to hardest: Indian Summer, Powering the Hero, Sereja and Suffixes, Same Differences.

challenges.title: Data Structures: Build Your Own
challenges.description: Implement the structures yourself instead of using the library: a stack that knows its maximum, a queue made of two stacks, and reversing a linked list by moving pointers.

challenges.title: Data Structures: Pick the Right One
challenges.description: Each of these becomes easy with the right standard-library container: a queue, a priority queue, a map, a set, a stack. Decide which one before you write any code.

quizzes.title: Data Structures
quizzes.description: Five questions on stacks, linked lists, maps and priority queues. Answers are revealed after you submit.

questions.question: Which structure gives back the most recently added element first?
How long does looking up a key in a std::unordered_map take on average?
With std::map<std::string, int> m, what does reading m["plum"] do when "plum" isn't in the map?
answers: It returns 0 and leaves the map unchanged

questions.question: Why is adding to the front of a linked list O(1), while it's O(n) for a vector?
answers: Only one new node is created and one pointer changed; a vector has to shift every element

questions.question: You need the largest value of a collection again and again while values are added. Which structure fits best?

lessons.title: Data Structures
lessons.description:
How to organize data so the jobs you need are fast (about 40 minutes, after Introduction to Algorithms): vectors, stacks, queues, linked lists, sets, maps and priority queues, explained with everyday examples. Build a stack and a linked list yourself, then use the C++ standard library versions.

After the lesson, practise by topic ("Stacks & Queues", "Sets, Maps & Heaps") or by skill ("Build Your Own", "Pick the Right One") under Practice, and take the "Data Structures" quiz.
